title: Red-Black Tree
description: The same keys, in the same order, into two trees. Fed sorted keys, a plain search tree collapses into a long line; a red-black tree recolours and rotates as it goes and stays short and bushy.
long_description:
A binary search tree puts smaller keys to the left and larger keys to the right, so a search follows one path down. But feed it keys in sorted order and every key goes right: the “tree” becomes a list as tall as the data.

The red-black tree next to it follows two rules — no red node has a red child, and every path down passes the same number of black nodes. When a new key breaks a rule it recolours, or rotates three nodes around, and each rotation happens on screen. The heights at the bottom are the punchline.

Those rules keep the height under 2·log₂ n. Java’s TreeMap, C++’s std::map and the Linux scheduler all use red-black trees.
action_hints: insert keys in sorted order and watch the plain tree fall over
insert the same keys in random order
insert one key and follow its rotations
